# DDR-164: BYOK AI media generation — provider-adapter spine, key custody, trust boundary

**Status:** Accepted — 2026-07-11 (Phase 0 implemented via `/flow:execute`, plan `.ai/plans/feature-ai-media-generation.md`). Phases 1–5 (image breadth · audio · video · proactive · local engines) are staged follow-ups on this spine.
**Extends:** [DDR-088](DDR-088-canvas-media-vocabulary-and-asset-write-surface.md) (the content-addressed `assets/<sha8>` write surface every generated byte lands in — `saveAsset`'s magic-byte sniff + category cap is the localizer's gate), [DDR-054](DDR-054-linked-mode-trust-model-and-task-4-hardening.md) (the generation routes are main-origin-only, absent from both canvas allowlists — a provider key must never cross into the untrusted canvas realm), [DDR-108](DDR-108-github-token-keychain-loopback-bridge.md) (the fetch-at-request-time, never-cache, null-outside-the-app key-resolution template `getGithubToken`, mirrored by `getProviderKey`).
**Related:** [DDR-115](DDR-115-per-user-camera-split-and-runtime-state-taxonomy.md) (the `_generate-history.json` job ledger is per-machine runtime state — added to all three ignore lists; generated assets themselves are VERSIONED in `assets/`), [DDR-062](DDR-062-plugins-reach-executable-logic-via-maude.md) (the `generate` verb dispatches via `maude design`), [DDR-161](DDR-161-in-app-photo-editor-webgl-pipeline-and-photoedit-sidecar.md) (a generated image is a valid `PhotoEdit.source` — Phase 1 wires image-gen into the parametric editor), [DDR-148](DDR-148-video-comp-remotion-authoring-capture-export.md)/[DDR-163](DDR-163-footage-analysis-director-layer.md) (a generated clip becomes an `EdlBeat.clip` — Phase 3), [DDR-123](DDR-123-native-agent-chat-acp-sidepanel.md) (generation keys must not leak into the ACP `claude` subprocess env).
**Instruments (Phase 0):** `apps/studio/generation/{types,keys,registry,download,jobs}.ts` + `adapters/gemini.ts`, `apps/studio/http.ts` (`/_api/generate-jobs` + `/_api/generate/providers` + `/_api/generate/keys` routes) + `apps/studio/server.ts` (queue wiring) + `apps/studio/ws.ts` (`generate:job` push), `apps/studio/config.schema.json` + `apps/studio/context.ts` (`generation` block), `apps/studio/client/panels/SettingsPanel.jsx` + `apps/studio/client/generate-dialog.jsx` + `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` (menubar/palette/⌘,), `apps/studio/bin/generate.sh` + `cli/commands/design.mjs` (BIN_VERBS), the DDR-115 triple-list (`git/service.ts` + `cli/lib/gitignore-block.mjs` + `.gitignore`), `apps/studio/test/canvas-origin-gate.test.ts` + `generate-route.test.ts` + `generation/*.test.ts`.

## Context

Maude can arrange, edit, and export media (photo-editor DDR-161, footage→director→reel DDR-163, video-comp DDR-148, content-addressed `assets/` + `/_api/asset` DDR-088) but had **zero ability to create net-new media**. Claude Code itself cannot generate pixels/audio, so this is entirely external-provider (+ optional local-model) work. The user wants to bring their own provider keys (Google Nano Banana, ElevenLabs, fal.ai) and generate images/video/audio/captions inside Maude — which needs a provider abstraction, key custody, a Settings UI, and a route seam, none of which existed.

## Decision — normalize every provider to one `submit → Job → assets[]` contract

`apps/studio/generation/` is a provider-adapter spine. Three adapter *shapes* cover ~80% of providers — `direct` (Gemini/ElevenLabs — small, sync-ish), `fal-queue` (fal aggregator — async poll/SSE), `openai-compatible` (OpenAI + local Ollama/whisper-server) — all behind one `ProviderAdapter` interface. Phase 0 ships the whole spine end-to-end proven with the **simplest** modality: **image via Google Nano Banana** (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`) — synchronous, single REST call, base64 out, drops into the existing asset spine with almost no new surface.

### 1. Hybrid provider strategy (direct BYOK + one aggregator), never a hosted router

Direct adapters for the flagship providers the user named (truest BYOK, no aggregator markup, the user's own key → the provider directly) **plus** fal.ai for breadth. fal is called **directly from the machine** (Type-A BYOK — fal bills the user's own account), never a hosted router: OpenRouter/Vercel-AI-Gateway are deliberately NOT a required spine dependency, because they insert a hosted dependency that contradicts the local/private premise (they can drop in later as optional `openai-compatible`-family adapters). **Poll/SSE, never webhooks** — a laptop has no public URL.

### 2. The sync/async seam is hidden — every provider returns a `Job`

`submit()` returns immediately even for a synchronous provider: Gemini's single round-trip is wrapped in an **already-`done` Job** so the host queue (and every caller) treats sync and async uniformly. Output normalizes to `GenResult.assets[]`, and **every produced byte localizes into `assets/<sha8>.<ext>`** through `download.ts` → `api.saveAsset` (magic-byte sniff + category cap — the same tested path drag-drop upload uses). Expiring provider URLs (fal/Veo) MUST be downloaded before they're referenced anywhere; the Phase-0 URL branch **fails loud** rather than shipping an unhardened egress path (the SSRF-hardened URL localizer lands with fal in Phase 1).

### 3. Key custody — request-time resolution, never cached, never echoed

A provider key lives OUTSIDE the served `.design/` tree — in the OS keychain (native, Phase 5) or `~/.config/maude/keys.json` mode **0600** (browser, Phase 0) — and is resolved **at request time inside the job's `run`** (`getProviderKey`, the `getGithubToken` template: fetch-at-use, never cache, null when absent). It is injected into the adapter via `AdapterContext.apiKey` and used ONLY in the provider request header — **never in a URL query** (so it can't leak via a redirect `Location` or an echoed error string). The Settings panel POSTs a key to the privileged `/_api/generate/keys` route, which **never echoes it back**: GET returns only `{ configured: [...] }` (presence, mirroring `github_is_signed_in`). Verified live: after saving a key, `GET /_api/generate/keys` returns `{"configured":["gemini"]}` with the secret absent; the on-disk file is mode 0600.

### 4. The generation routes are main-origin-only (privileged)

`/_api/generate-jobs` (+ `/providers` + `/keys`) resolve a provider KEY and make outbound provider calls — the untrusted canvas iframe must never reach them; it sees only the produced `/assets/<sha8>`. All three are **absent from both canvas allowlists** (`CANVAS_SAFE_API` + `startCanvasServer` routes), loopback-`Host` gated on every method, and the mutating POST/DELETE are additionally `sameOriginWrite` CSRF-gated. `canvas-origin-gate.test.ts` asserts a `GET → 403` from the canvas origin for all three (route unreachable, not 405 from a reached handler).

### 5. The job queue mirrors the export queue; assets are the durable output

`generation/jobs.ts` clones `exporters/jobs.ts` (counting semaphore, in-memory Map, `MAX_PENDING` backpressure → 429, `generate:job` bus push → notification center). Unlike exports there is **no per-job byte store** — a generation's output is a set of `assets/<sha8>` rel paths already in the durable content-addressed store; the only on-disk state is a small `_generate-history.json` ledger (DDR-115 runtime state, all three ignore lists), so the notification center survives a restart.

### 6. Config carries non-secret preferences only

The `generation` block in `config.json` (`defaultImageProvider`, `defaultModels`, `preferLocalWhenAvailable`, per-provider `enabled`/`localEndpoint`) is **non-secret only** — provider keys are NEVER in the committed config. `additionalProperties:false` at every level rejects a stray secret field (Ajv-verified). It's hot-reloadable via the existing full in-place `ctx.cfg` swap in `reloadConfig` (only `designRoot`/`linkedHub` are boot-pinned), so Settings saves take effect without a restart.

## Consequences

- **Adding a provider = one registry entry** (a factory + descriptor + static model list); no route change. Phase 1 adds fal, Phase 2 ElevenLabs, etc.
- **`maude design generate`** joins the DDR-062 BIN_VERBS — a thin non-browser curl → `/_api/generate-jobs` → poll → print `/assets/<sha8>.<ext>` (the provider call is server-side, so no client-side inference/harness, unlike `photo-bg-remove`). Ships via `apps/studio` in `package.json` `files` (already covered).
- **Prompt-injection posture (Phases 1/4):** the proactive director reads canvas/footage content that could carry injected instructions → canvas text is data, never tool-authorizing; the director only *proposes* a plan artifact, the command executes after one `AskUserQuestion`, generation never runs unattended.
- **Licensing/consent** (music commercial-rights tier, voice-cloning consent, SynthID watermark) is surfaced in the Settings UI via the descriptor `notes` — a per-provider inert copy field, not a runtime gate.
- **Explicitly avoided:** OpenAI Sora 2 (API sunsets 2026-09-24) and Suno/Udio (no official API — grey-market wrappers only).
- **Live end-to-end image generation with a real Google key is the owner's live-gate** — the spine is fully unit- + integration- + live-UI-verified minus the real provider call (stubbed HTTP proves the adapter path).

## Security fan-out (Phase 0) — findings + resolution

A defender (`security-auditor`) + adversarial (`ethical-hacker`) pass ran on the new egress + secret + route surface. The core origin-split + CSRF + write-only key custody design was found sound and **tested** (canvas 403, no key ever crosses to the client — even a hypothetical main-origin XSS could only *spend*, not steal). Two Medium findings were **fixed in Phase 0**:

- **F1 (Medium — RAM DoS) — FIXED.** The Gemini adapter buffered the provider response with `res.json()` + `Buffer.from(base64)` before `saveAsset`'s cap (which only guards the *disk* write) could fire — a multi-GB upstream body could OOM-crash the shared server. Now `readTextCapped` bounds the response (Content-Length reject + streamed-size cap, `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` default 64 MB) before decode; the base64 is bounded transitively. Test: `gemini.test.ts` "an over-cap response body is rejected".
- **F2 (Medium — key-egress redirect / SSRF) — FIXED.** `MAUDE_GEMINI_API_BASE` had no scheme/host allowlist, so a poisoned env could redirect the BYOK key to an attacker/internal host. `assertSafeBase` now requires `https:` + the fixed host `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, with an explicit `MAUDE_GEN_ALLOW_CUSTOM_BASE=1` opt-in for a test mock. Test: `gemini.test.ts` "a non-allowlisted base is refused".

Two follow-ups are **tracked, not yet actioned** (below the Phase-0 bar or out of scope):

- **F3 (Low now → High at Phase 5.1) — BROUGHT FORWARD + FIXED in Phase 1.** When the native keychain bridge is wired (`keychainBridgeAvailable()` is inert in Phase 0), its `MAUDE_GEN_KEY_ENDPOINT` + `MAUDE_GEN_KEY_KEY` env vars would become inheritable by the ACP `claude` subprocess (DDR-123) — a prompt-injected agent could read them and query the loopback keychain bridge for every provider key. Phase 1 wires the ACP↔generation link (Task 1.4), so rather than leave the tripwire disarmed until Phase 5.1, `acp/env.ts` now scrubs the whole `MAUDE_GEN_KEY*` custody namespace (bridge endpoint + key, plus `MAUDE_GEN_KEYS_PATH`) **before** the bridge exists — the ACP child never needs them (the sidecar, a separate process, resolves keys). Test: `test/acp-env.test.ts` "scrubs the generation key-custody env vars". **Honest residual (ethical-hacker Phase-1 pass):** this does NOT make a provider key unreadable to a *compromised same-OS-user agent* — a full-tool ACP agent runs as the user and could read the default `~/.config/maude/keys.json` (0600, owner = that user) off disk like any other file it owns. That is the pre-existing full-tool-agent **trifecta** (untrusted-content-in + private-data-on-disk + outbound-tools), NOT something an env-scrub can close and NOT newly created by generation; it is accepted, and the `ai-generation` skill's "one rule" section states it plainly rather than claiming (as an earlier Phase-1 draft did) that the env-scrub makes the key safe. The scrub's job is narrower and real: never *hand* the child a key or a bridge pointer it doesn't need.
- **F4 (Low — cost ceiling).** The queue bounds concurrency + pending depth but not spend-over-time; only reachable as an amplifier chained to a hypothetical future main-origin shell-XSS (the write-only key design caps the worst case at "money drain," never key theft). A rolling per-hour job/cost ceiling with a surfaced counter is a defense-in-depth follow-up.
- **Phase 4 (trifecta).** The proactive "director" completes the lethal-trifecta loop (private data + outbound channel are already present; Phase 4 adds untrusted-content-driven prompts). Phase 4 MUST human-gate the director's outbound generation — untrusted canvas text must never drive a billed egress without a confirm (already the plan's one-`AskUserQuestion` posture; recorded here as a hard security requirement).
